# Disposable component fixture

Only for loopback synthetic tests; never deploy these public fixture wrappers to an app or cloud. The candidate archive is not selected by the application. Create a fresh directory, copy this directory's `convex/` and `package.json`, extract `vendor/convex-auth-437831bd-disposabl.5.tgz` into `authpkg/`, append `google-bridge.ts.txt` to `authpkg/src/components/google/provider.ts` and `password-seed.ts.txt` to `authpkg/src/components/password/public.ts`, and link the local installed dependencies into `authpkg/node_modules` and fixture `node_modules`. Start an anonymous local Convex backend on free ports 3540/3541 with telemetry disabled and set `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` inside it. The bridge and seed are fixture-only and are not shipped in the candidate archive.

Using the wrappers, create an authorization before a cutoff and one after, call `bridge` only after the cutoff, then concurrently call `redeem` twice per ticket: assert the stored markers straddle the cutoff and exactly one claim per ticket succeeds. For passwords, race `erasePassword` with `setPassword`, verify the old ID rejects both verification and further writes, verify another ID and a fresh ID remain usable, and retry erasure. The seed wrapper can insert 201 duplicate synthetic rows; four erase calls must report deleted counts 100,100,1,0 and complete flags false,false,true,true. These tests use no provider and establish only component transaction behavior, not core account erasure or a Google identity cutoff.

For the `.6` core test, extract the `.6` archive instead, also append `core-seed.ts.txt` to `authpkg/src/component/public.ts`, start the same isolated backend and run `python3 core-test.py`. The test-only core seed creates synthetic records, including an orphan refresh token, to prove the API reports the unresolved legacy-orphan boundary. `beginBoth` invokes the real core and password component mutations inside one app mutation. No fixture-only helper ships in the archive.

For `.7`, extract that archive, append all three fixture-only bridge/seed files as above, and run `python3 identity-test.py` against the isolated backend. The fixture's synthetic Google ticket is encrypted and inserted by a test-only component bridge; no Google endpoint is contacted. The real redemption mutation, component-owned identity cutoff and core mutations are exercised. The test checks receipt creation in the session-deletion transaction; it does not establish that historical orphan tokens can be attributed or erased. The fixture wrappers are public and must never be deployed to a shared or production backend.

`product-test.py` invokes the real product `users.authDeletion.runBatch` through a fixture-only wrapper and the installed `.7` components. It checks concurrent operator batches and counters, stale requests and another user, authenticated session and password denial, linked cleanup, identity cutoff, and repeat completion. The fixture's `auth.config.ts` validates synthetic access tokens. This remains a local-only test and does not establish remote drain, historical orphan cleanup, or complete deletion.
